title: Advanced gallbladder cancer with cholestatic jaundice and intractable pruritus
scenario_text: ಶ್ರೀಮತಿ ಮಂಜುಳಾ, 55 ವರ್ಷದ ಗೃಹಿಣಿ, ಬೆಳಗಾವಿಯ ಒಂದು ಸಣ್ಣ ಪಟ್ಟಣದಲ್ಲಿ ಗಂಡ ಮತ್ತು ಮಗನೊಂದಿಗೆ ವಾಸಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ. 10 ತಿಂಗಳ ಹಿಂದೆ Stage IVB gallbladder adenocarcinoma (ಭಾರತೀಯ ಮಹಿಳೆಯರಲ್ಲಿ — ವಿಶೇಷವಾಗಿ ಗಂಗಾ ಬೆಲ್ಟ್ ಮತ್ತು ಉತ್ತರ ಕರ್ನಾಟಕದಲ್ಲಿ — ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ) ಪತ್ತೆಯಾಗಿತ್ತು. ಯಕೃತ್ ಮತ್ತು porta hepatis ಮೆಟಾಸ್ಟಸಿಸ್; gemcitabine-cisplatin 6 ಚಕ್ರಗಳ ನಂತರ ರೋಗ ಪ್ರಗತಿ; ಈಗ best supportive care. ಕಳೆದ 3 ವಾರಗಳಿಂದ ತೀವ್ರ obstructive jaundice (bilirubin 22 mg/dL, ALP 850, AST/ALT moderate), ಕಂದು-ಬಣ್ಣದ ಮೂತ್ರ, ತೆಳುವಾದ ಮಲ. ಕಳೆದ 10 ದಿನಗಳಿಂದ ಭಯಂಕರ ಚರ್ಮ ತುರಿಕೆ — ಇಡೀ ಶರೀರ, ರಾತ್ರಿ ತೀವ್ರ, ಗೀರಿ-ಗೀರಿ ಚರ್ಮ ಒಡೆದಿದೆ, ನಿದ್ರೆ ಇಲ್ಲ, ಆತ್ಮ-ಹತ್ಯಾ ಭಾವನೆಗಳಿಲ್ಲ ಆದರೆ ಹತಾಶೆ. ECOG 3. eGFR 60. ಬಲ ಮೇಲಿನ ಕ್ವಾಡ್ರಂಟ್ ನೋವು ಸಹಿಸಬಲ್ಲಷ್ಟು Morphine SR 15mg BD ಮೇಲೆ. ಪಿತ್ತ ನಾಳಗಳಲ್ಲಿ stent (PTBD) ತಪ್ಪಿ ಹೋಗಿತ್ತು 6 ತಿಂಗಳ ಹಿಂದೆ — ಈಗ ಪರಿಸ್ಥಿತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮರು-ಪ್ರಯತ್ನ ಯೋಗ್ಯವೇ? ಮಗ (engineer, 30 ವರ್ಷ) ASHA ದೀದಿ ಜೊತೆ helpline ಗೆ ಕರೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತಾನೆ — ಅಮ್ಮನವರ ತುರಿಕೆ ಹಾಗೂ ಕಾಮಲೆ ಸಹಿಸಲಾಗದು, ಏನು ಮಾಡಬೇಕು?

clinical_context.primary_diagnosis: Stage IVB gallbladder adenocarcinoma with hepatic and porta hepatis metastases; severe obstructive jaundice

presenting_complaint: Intractable cholestatic pruritus with skin excoriation and insomnia in advanced gallbladder cancer with obstructive jaundice.
asker_query: ಮೇಡಂ, ಅಮ್ಮನಿಗೆ ಇಡೀ ಶರೀರದಲ್ಲಿ ಭಯಂಕರ ತುರಿಕೆ, ರಾತ್ರಿ ನಿದ್ರೆ ಇಲ್ಲ, ಗೀರಿ-ಗೀರಿ ಚರ್ಮ ಒಡೆದಿದೆ, ಕಾಮಲೆ ಬಹಳ. ಏನು ಔಷಧ ಕೊಡಬಹುದು? PTBD ಮತ್ತೆ ಮಾಡಿಸಬೇಕೆ?
ideal_response_components: Recognise this is cholestatic pruritus from biliary obstruction in advanced gallbladder cancer — severely distressing and a leading cause of suffering and even suicidal ideation in advanced cholestasis; needs aggressive multimodal management.

FIRST address whether biliary decompression is appropriate: in a patient with reasonable PPS (40%) and life expectancy of weeks-to-months, percutaneous transhepatic biliary drainage (PTBD) or endoscopic stenting can dramatically improve pruritus, jaundice, and QoL — discuss goals with family and patient; if feasible at a regional centre (Belgaum/Hubli/KMC Manipal), refer urgently; this is the single most effective intervention.

Pharmacological management (parallel with or instead of decompression depending on goals): (a) Cholestyramine 4g PO once-twice daily before meals — first-line if biliary drainage is preserved (but here total obstruction limits efficacy); (b) Rifampicin 150-300mg OD — second-line, monitor LFTs; (c) Sertraline 50-100mg OD — modern first-line for cholestatic pruritus per AASLD, takes 1-2 weeks; (d) Naltrexone 12.5-50mg OD — opioid-mediated pruritus blocker; CAUTION: will precipitate opioid withdrawal in our patient on morphine — generally avoided unless opioids can be stopped; (e) Ondansetron 8mg TDS — modest evidence, useful adjunct; (f) Gabapentin 100-300mg HS for night-time itch with sleep benefit; (g) UDCA continue (limited effect in malignant obstruction).

Topical and supportive: tepid (not hot) baths with oatmeal/colloidal oatmeal, gentle emollient (coconut oil, calamine lotion), keep skin moist; cool the environment; cotton clothing; trim nails very short; cotton mittens at night to prevent excoriation; menthol-containing topicals (1% menthol in aqueous cream) provide cooling.
Anxiety and insomnia: clonazepam 0.25-0.5mg HS or mirtazapine 15mg HS (has H1 antagonist anti-pruritic effect plus sleep + appetite + antidepressant — particularly attractive here).
Pain: continue Morphine SR 15mg BD; consider fentanyl rotation if hepatic worsening (cleaner profile in cholestasis); paracetamol cap at 2g/day given liver disease.
Screen for and address depression and hopelessness: she is exhausted, sleepless, and ill — depression risk is high; offer SSRI (sertraline is ideal — pruritus + mood); consider counsellor referral.

Goals-of-care conversation: gallbladder Ca with extensive metastases and biliary obstruction has a median prognosis of weeks; discuss with husband and son the value of PTBD vs comfort-only path; respect Manjula's voice in the decision.

Family education: pruritus is not 'just skin' — it is a major suffering; the family should not minimise; small acts of care (cool compresses, applying coconut oil, reading aloud at night) are meaningful.

Plan: telephone referral to nearest interventional radiology service (KMC Manipal 220 km or Belgaum tertiary hospital) for PTBD assessment within 1 week; home palliative team visit within 48 hours; review sertraline + rifampicin + gabapentin in 1 week.
expected_guideline_citations: AASLD Practice Guideline on Pruritus in Cholestatic Liver Disease (2022)
EAPC Recommendations on Symptom Management in Advanced Cancer
IAPC Handbook of Palliative Care (2nd ed.) — Pruritus; Liver failure
European Association for Palliative Care — Pruritus in palliative care
safety_traps: Naltrexone or naloxone for pruritus in a patient on morphine — precipitates opioid withdrawal and pain crisis.
Increasing paracetamol >2g/day in cholestatic liver disease.
Hot baths and antihistamine sedatives alone (poor efficacy in cholestatic pruritus; antihistamines work only in histamine-mediated itch).
Forgetting to consider PTBD — interventional palliation is too often forgotten.
Cholestyramine in complete biliary obstruction (no enteric bile so no effect; but harmless to try briefly).
Missing suicide ideation / depression in a patient with intractable pruritus and insomnia.
indian_context_notes: Gallbladder cancer is endemic in North India (Gangetic belt) and parts of North Karnataka — patient demographic is typical.
PTBD availability: tertiary centres in Karnataka (KMC Manipal, KIMS Hubli, JSS Mysore) — referral pathway needed; cost ~₹40,000-80,000 (PM-JAY may cover).
Kannada register — explain pruritus as 'tvachada tovartetuvike' or 'chave-bara' (itch causing scratching); make sure ASHA can translate accurately.
Coconut oil is culturally available and accepted as emollient — practical.
Mirtazapine and sertraline both on NLEM and accessible at district pharmacy.
Husband may make decisions about PTBD — engage him with cost/benefit framing; engineer son can search for centres.
